newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on hedge selling, rainfall.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on hedge selling, rainfall.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on commercial selling, tied to hedge selling, traders said.
ABN Amro-The Chicago Corp sold six million bushels of December, Cargill Investor Services sold four million Dec and Cargill Inc sold two million bushels of Dec, traders said.
Also one key fund was a noted seller which contributed pressure with Prudential Securities a featured seller of five million bushels of December, traders said.

Recent rains in key U.S. Midwest corn areas should help boost the corn crop's ear filling and the market also fell Thursday on USDA's weekly export sales report which showed the corn number well below expectations.

However, declines were curbed by news Taiwan overnight bought 216,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and position squaring was noted before the weekend and ahead of the release late Friday of USDA's Cattle on Feed Report.

USDA said the number of cattle placed on feed in the seven key U.S. cattle feeding states was 18 percent above a year ago, compared with an average analysts' estimate for only an 0.8 percent increase.
Corn ended two to 5-1/2 cents a bushel lower, with September down 4-1/4 at $2.60.
In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of December/September at 3-1/2 cents, premium December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 47,500 contracts, below the 61,845 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 December $2.50 puts at six cents, SAK Futures bought 400 December $2.90 calls at 6-1/4 cents and Lind Waldock sold 450 December $2.70 calls at 10-1/4 cents and sold 450 December $2.70 puts at 16-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 25,486 traded Thursday.
